findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous when names or folder UIDs contain '_'.
findings.body: The key joins `name` and `parent` with `_`, and dashboard and folder UIDs may contain `_`. So dashboard `a_b` in folder `c` and dashboard `a` in folder `b_c` both map to `...perm_<uid>_<action>_a_b_c`. A denial for one makes Check deny the other without asking the DB, which is a false denial of a resource the user can access. Fix: use a separator that cannot appear in UIDs, or length-prefix or escape each part.

findings.title: Cached denials are never invalidated, so a fresh grant stays denied for the cache TTL.
findings.body: A denial is written for `shortCacheTTL` and is checked before any DB lookup. Nothing clears it when permissions change. Trigger: a user (often the creator) is checked against a dashboard or folder before its permission rows are written, for example while the UI loads the new resource or during the save-then-set-permissions window. They can also be checked just before an admin grants access. Every later Check for the same user/action/name/folder returns `Allowed:false` without querying the DB until the entry expires. That is the stale-access problem this PR sets out to fix. Fix: do not cache denials in this path, give them a much shorter TTL, or invalidate them when permissions are written.

held.title: The denial-cache test seeds a `false` permission, so it may pass even without the denial cache.
held.body: The comment says the cached entry should allow access, which would prove the denial cache short-circuits the check. But the map value is `false`. If `checkPermission` reads the value, the cached path denies, the DB fallback (empty fakeStore) also denies, and the test passes with the denial cache removed. I could not see whether `checkPermission` reads the value or only checks that the key exists. Fix: set `"dashboards:uid:dash1": true` so the test actually covers the denial cache.
